questions.q: A first-order gas-phase reaction $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$ takes place in a constant volume vessel. Initially, the vessel contains a mixture of reactant gas $\mathrm{A}$ and an unreactive (inert) gas. The initial total pressure of the mixture at $t=0$ is $200 \text{ mm Hg}$. The total pressure after $20 \text{ minutes}$ is $280 \text{ mm Hg}$, and the total pressure after a very long time ($t \rightarrow \infty$) is $500 \text{ mm Hg}$. The partial pressure of gas $\mathrm{A}$ after $20 \text{ minutes}$ is:
questions.question: A first-order gas-phase reaction $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$ takes place in a constant volume vessel. Initially, the vessel contains a mixture of reactant gas $\mathrm{A}$ and an unreactive (inert) gas. The initial total pressure of the mixture at $t=0$ is $200 \text{ mm Hg}$. The total pressure after $20 \text{ minutes}$ is $280 \text{ mm Hg}$, and the total pressure after a very long time ($t \rightarrow \infty$) is $500 \text{ mm Hg}$. The partial pressure of gas $\mathrm{A}$ after $20 \text{ minutes}$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $P_0$ be the initial partial pressure of gas $\mathrm{A}$ and $P_I$ be the partial pressure of the inert gas.

At $t = 0$, the total pressure is the sum of the partial pressures:
$P_0 + P_I = 200 \text{ mm Hg}$ --- (Equation 1)

At $t \rightarrow \infty$, all of gas $\mathrm{A}$ has decomposed. Since $1$ mole of $\mathrm{A}$ yields $3$ moles of gaseous products ($2\mathrm{B} + \mathrm{C}$), the final partial pressure of the products will be $3P_0$. The inert gas pressure remains unchanged.
Total pressure at $t \rightarrow \infty$ is:
$3P_0 + P_I = 500 \text{ mm Hg}$ --- (Equation 2)

Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:
$(3P_0 + P_I) - (P_0 + P_I) = 500 - 200$
$2P_0 = 300 \Rightarrow P_0 = 150 \text{ mm Hg}$
Substituting $P_0$ back into Equation 1 gives $P_I = 50 \text{ mm Hg}$.

At $t = 20 \text{ minutes}$, let $x$ be the decrease in the partial pressure of $\mathrm{A}$.
Partial pressure of $\mathrm{A} = P_0 - x$
Partial pressure of $\mathrm{B} = 2x$
Partial pressure of $\mathrm{C} = x$
Total pressure $P_t = (P_0 - x) + 2x + x + P_I = P_0 + 2x + P_I$

Since $P_0 + P_I = 200$, we have:
$P_t = 200 + 2x$
Given $P_t = 280 \text{ mm Hg}$ at $t = 20 \text{ minutes}$:
$200 + 2x = 280 \Rightarrow 2x = 80 \Rightarrow x = 40 \text{ mm Hg}$

The partial pressure of gas $\mathrm{A}$ after $20 \text{ minutes}$ is:
$P_A = P_0 - x = 150 - 40 = 110 \text{ mm Hg}$.

Answer: $110 \text{ mm Hg}$

questions.q: The rate constants for two different reactions are given by $k_1 = A e^{-2000/T}$ and $k_2 = A e \cdot e^{-2500/T}$, where the temperature $T$ is in Kelvin. The temperature at which both reactions have the same rate constant is ____ K.
questions.question: The rate constants for two different reactions are given by $k_1 = A e^{-2000/T}$ and $k_2 = A e \cdot e^{-2500/T}$, where the temperature $T$ is in Kelvin. The temperature at which both reactions have the same rate constant is ____ K.
questions.solution:
Given the rate constants for the two reactions:
$k_1 = A e^{-2000/T}$
$k_2 = A e \cdot e^{-2500/T} = A e^{1 - 2500/T}$

We need to find the temperature $T$ at which $k_1 = k_2$:
$A e^{-2000/T} = A e^{1 - 2500/T}$

Cancelling the pre-exponential factor $A$ from both sides:
$e^{-2000/T} = e^{1 - 2500/T}$

Equating the exponents:
$-\dfrac{2000}{T} = 1 - \dfrac{2500}{T}$

Rearranging the terms:
$\dfrac{2500}{T} - \dfrac{2000}{T} = 1$

$\dfrac{500}{T} = 1$

$T = 500$ K

Answer: $500$

questions.q: Substances P and Q undergo first-order radioactive decay in a container. The initial concentration of P is $16$ times that of Q. The half-life of P is $10\text{ min}$. If both start decaying at the same time and after exactly $60\text{ min}$, their concentrations become equal, the half-life of Q is ________ min.
questions.question: Substances P and Q undergo first-order radioactive decay in a container. The initial concentration of P is $16$ times that of Q. The half-life of P is $10\text{ min}$. If both start decaying at the same time and after exactly $60\text{ min}$, their concentrations become equal, the half-life of Q is ________ min.
questions.solution:
For a first-order decay, the concentration at time $t$ is given by:
$[A]_t = [A]_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{t}{t_{1/2}}}$

For substance P:
$[P]_t = [P]_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{60}{10}} = [P]_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^6 = \dfrac{[P]_0}{64}$

Given that $[P]_0 = 16[Q]_0$, we can substitute this into the equation for P:
$[P]_t = \dfrac{16[Q]_0}{64} = \dfrac{[Q]_0}{4}$

For substance Q:
$[Q]_t = [Q]_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{60}{t_{1/2, Q}}}$

Since the concentrations are equal at $60\text{ min}$, $[P]_t = [Q]_t$:
$\dfrac{[Q]_0}{4} = [Q]_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{60}{t_{1/2, Q}}}$

$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{60}{t_{1/2, Q}}}$

Equating the exponents:
$\dfrac{60}{t_{1/2, Q}} = 2$

$t_{1/2, Q} = 30\text{ min}$

Answer: $30$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $x\%$ completion is exactly twice the time required for $90\%$ completion. The value of $x$ is:
questions.question: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $x\%$ completion is exactly twice the time required for $90\%$ completion. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, the time $t$ required for a certain percentage completion is given by the integrated rate law:
$t = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln\left(\dfrac{100}{100 - \text{percentage}}\right)$

The time required for $90\%$ completion is:
$t_{90\%} = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln\left(\dfrac{100}{100 - 90}\right) = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln(10)$

The time required for $x\%$ completion is given as twice $t_{90\%}$:
$t_{x\%} = 2 \times t_{90\%} = \dfrac{2}{k} \ln(10) = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln(10^2) = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln(100)$

Equating this to the standard formula for $x\%$ completion:
$\dfrac{1}{k} \ln\left(\dfrac{100}{100 - x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{k} \ln(100)$

$\dfrac{100}{100 - x} = 100$

$100 - x = 1$

$x = 99$

Answer: 99

Match List I with List II.

B. Slope of $\log k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ plotII. Fraction of molecules having kinetic energy $\ge E_a$

D. Factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$IV. $\ln A$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
A. Slope of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ plotI. $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303R}$
B. Slope of $\log k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ plotII. Fraction of molecules having kinetic energy $\ge E_a$
C. Intercept of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ plotIII. $-\dfrac{E_a}{R}$
D. Factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$IV. $\ln A$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The Arrhenius equation is given by $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$.

Taking the natural logarithm, we get $\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$.
Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, a plot of $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ has a slope of $-\dfrac{E_a}{R}$ and an intercept of $\ln A$. Thus, A matches with III and C matches with IV.

Converting to base 10 logarithm, we get $\log k = \log A - \dfrac{E_a}{2.303RT}$.
A plot of $\log k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ has a slope of $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303R}$. Thus, B matches with I.

The exponential factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$ represents the fraction of molecules that possess kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy $E_a$. Thus, D matches with II.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.q: Two compounds $A$ and $B$ in a flask decompose independently to yield the same product $P$. The reaction for $A$ is $A \rightarrow P$ and for $B$ is $B \rightarrow 2P$. Both reactions follow first-order kinetics. The half-life of $A$ is $20\text{ minutes}$ and that of $B$ is $40\text{ minutes}$. If the initial amounts of $A$ and $B$ are $400\text{ mmol}$ and $200\text{ mmol}$ respectively, the total amount of product $P$ formed after $40\text{ minutes}$ is ____ $\text{mmol}$.
questions.question: Two compounds $A$ and $B$ in a flask decompose independently to yield the same product $P$. The reaction for $A$ is $A \rightarrow P$ and for $B$ is $B \rightarrow 2P$. Both reactions follow first-order kinetics. The half-life of $A$ is $20\text{ minutes}$ and that of $B$ is $40\text{ minutes}$. If the initial amounts of $A$ and $B$ are $400\text{ mmol}$ and $200\text{ mmol}$ respectively, the total amount of product $P$ formed after $40\text{ minutes}$ is ____ $\text{mmol}$.
questions.solution:
For compound $A$, the number of half-lives passed in $40\text{ minutes}$ is $n_A = \dfrac{40}{20} = 2$.

Amount of $A$ remaining after $40\text{ minutes} = \dfrac{400}{2^2} = 100\text{ mmol}$.

Amount of $A$ reacted $= 400 - 100 = 300\text{ mmol}$.

From the stoichiometry $A \rightarrow P$, $1\text{ mole}$ of $A$ gives $1\text{ mole}$ of $P$.
Amount of $P$ formed from $A = 300\text{ mmol}$.

For compound $B$, the number of half-lives passed in $40\text{ minutes}$ is $n_B = \dfrac{40}{40} = 1$.

Amount of $B$ remaining after $40\text{ minutes} = \dfrac{200}{2^1} = 100\text{ mmol}$.

Amount of $B$ reacted $= 200 - 100 = 100\text{ mmol}$.

From the stoichiometry $B \rightarrow 2P$, $1\text{ mole}$ of $B$ gives $2\text{ moles}$ of $P$.
Amount of $P$ formed from $B = 100 \times 2 = 200\text{ mmol}$.

Total amount of product $P$ formed $= 300 + 200 = 500\text{ mmol}$.

Answer: $500$

questions.question:
A chemical reaction is carried out with and without a catalyst at $300\text{ K}$. The rate constant of the catalyzed reaction is $e^8$ times the rate constant of the uncatalyzed reaction. If the activation energy of the catalyzed reaction is $50\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, the activation energy of the uncatalyzed reaction is ________ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

[Given: $R = \dfrac{25}{3}\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, assume the pre-exponential factor $A$ remains the same for both reactions]
questions.solution:
According to the Arrhenius equation, the rate constant is given by $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$.

For the catalyzed and uncatalyzed reactions, we have:
$k_c = A e^{-E_{ac}/RT}$
$k_u = A e^{-E_{au}/RT}$

Dividing the two equations gives:
$\dfrac{k_c}{k_u} = e^{(E_{au} - E_{ac})/RT}$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:
$\ln\left(\dfrac{k_c}{k_u}\right) = \dfrac{E_{au} - E_{ac}}{RT}$

Given that $\dfrac{k_c}{k_u} = e^8$, we have $\ln(e^8) = 8$.

Substituting the given values ($T = 300\text{ K}$, $R = \dfrac{25}{3}\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $E_{ac} = 50\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 50000\text{ J mol}^{-1}$):
$8 = \dfrac{E_{au} - 50000}{\left(\dfrac{25}{3}\right) \times 300}$

$8 = \dfrac{E_{au} - 50000}{2500}$

$E_{au} - 50000 = 8 \times 2500 = 20000\text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$E_{au} = 50000 + 20000 = 70000\text{ J mol}^{-1} = 70\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $70$
